claims.text: The starting CoCrFeNi alloy has a relatively homogeneous, coarse-grained microstructure.
Minor Al and Nb additions to CoCrFeNi will trigger in-situ formation of nano-coupled grains and finely distributed nanoprecipitates.
The proposed alloying additions will induce composition undulation and a nanohierarchical architecture in CoCrFeNi.
A nanohierarchical architecture containing nano-coupled grains and nanoprecipitates can provide adaptive friction-interface protection over temperatures from room temperature to 800 °C.
The modified CoCrFeNi will develop a dense nanocrystalline glaze layer during elevated-temperature sliding.
At room temperature, multiple deformation pathways in the engineered nanostructure will dissipate or release frictional stress in stages.
At 800 °C, a dense nanocrystalline glaze layer will minimize adhesive and oxidative wear.
The proposed adaptive mechanisms will maintain reduced wear throughout the full range from approximately 25 °C to 800 °C.
The doped, nanostructured CoCrFeNi will have a significantly lower wear rate than undoped CoCrFeNi over the full temperature range.
The doped, nanostructured CoCrFeNi will have a significantly lower coefficient of friction than undoped CoCrFeNi over the full temperature range.
The expected performance improvement applies under both air and inert-gas sliding environments.
The optimal dopant concentrations and processing conditions have not yet been established.
The long-term stability of the nanoprecipitates and protective glaze layer during prolonged high-temperature sliding is uncertain.
